help.intro: The passive says what is done without saying who does it: Das Auto wird repariert (the car is being repaired), Hier wird Deutsch gesprochen (German is spoken here). It is everywhere on signs, in instructions and in news — which is why you need to recognise it early. It is built from werden in position 2 and the participle (the same Partizip II as the Perfekt) at the end: wird … repariert, werden … verkauft. werden agrees with the subject: Das Brot wird gebacken. Die Brötchen werden gebacken. If you do want to name the doer, von + dative: Die Rechnung wird vom Chef bezahlt. Later in the course you will build the passive in the past and with modals; here you learn to read it and to produce the simplest present form — both halves of it: wird or werden in position 2, and the participle at the end.
help.tips[0].title: werden + participle at the end
help.tips[0].text: Das Zimmer | wird | jeden Tag | geputzt. wird / werden take position 2; the participle closes the sentence. Singular subject → wird, plural → werden.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: The shop is opened at nine.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The tickets are sold at the counter.
help.tips[0].examples[2].en: The flowers are watered every day.
help.tips[0].trap: English builds the passive with 'be' (is repaired). German uses werden, not sein: 'Das Auto ist repariert' means it is already fixed (a state), 'wird repariert' means it is being fixed.
help.tips[0].check.q: Die Fenster ____ jede Woche geputzt. (the windows, plural)
help.tips[0].check.why: The subject die Fenster is plural, so werden goes in position 2 and the participle geputzt goes at the end.
help.tips[1].title: Nobody in particular — or von + dative
help.tips[1].text: Most passives leave the doer out; that is their point. To add one: von dem / vom / von der: Die Rechnung wird vom Chef bezahlt.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: The children are picked up by their grandma.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The parcel is brought by the neighbour.
help.tips[1].check.why: The doer comes after von, which takes the dative: die Lehrerin → von der Lehrerin. vom is only for der and das nouns.
help.tips[2].title: Where you'll read it
help.tips[2].text: Hier wird Deutsch gesprochen. Das Büro wird renoviert. Die Straße wird gesperrt. Das Fest wird im Garten gefeiert. Signs, notices, announcements, recipes (Das Gemüse wird geschnitten).
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: Attention: the road will be closed tomorrow.
help.tips[2].check.q: A sign on a door says: „Das Büro wird renoviert.“ What is happening?
help.tips[2].check.why: wird + participle is an action in progress: the work is still going on.
help.tips[3].title: werden is 'become': the thing becomes done
help.tips[3].text: Das Auto wird repariert — the car becomes repaired. Think of werden as 'is getting', and the participle as what it is getting.
help.tips[3].check.why: The bridge is 'getting built', so German uses werden. ist gebaut would mean it is already finished.
help.remember[0]: wird / werden at 2, participle last: the same bracket, a new helper.
help.context.en: At the bakery: at four in the morning the dough is made. Then the rolls are baked. At six the shop is opened, and the rolls are sold. In the evening everything is cleaned. The bread that isn't sold is given to the food bank.
help.mistakes[0].why: The action passive uses werden; ist repariert is a finished state.
help.mistakes[2].why: The participle is the last word.
help.hook: Read signs like 'Hier wird Deutsch gesprochen' and say what gets done without naming who does it.
